sentences.text: 1 Appellant's contention is that first appeal filed by the applicant was dismissed as it was informed that DNA report is positive, therefore, appellant has withdrawn the first appeal.
It is submitted that thereafter prosecutrix was examined before the trial Court on 02/07/2022 and it appears from her deposition that she was a consenting party.
First incident took place on 18/11/2021.
She was too much pregnant when she approached the appellant on 18/11/2021.

It is submitted that prosecutrix being major and a consenting party, in light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Tukaram and another Vs. The State of Maharashtra, (1079) 2 SCC 143 wherein it is held that offence is to be established by the prosecution beyond doubt.
Reliance is also placed on the decision of Delhi high Court in the case of Mahmood Farooqui Vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), 2017 SCC OnLine Del 63278 wherein reading paragraphs-84 to 86, it is submitted that what is the meaning of consent and how consent is to be inferred.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Mahmood Farooqui Vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), 2017 SCC OnLine Del 63278
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reading this judgment, it is submitted that since prosecutrix is a consenting party, therefore, it is a good case to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

It is further submitted by Shri Dhiraj Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, that place of incident is the clinic of the doctor which is a public place, prosecutrix neither shouted nor called for any help in the public place.
Prosecutrix was dragged.
She was threatened and she comes from under privilege family and since she was unconscious, her active consent cannot be adduced merely on the suggestion of counsel for the applicant.

Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Govt. Advocate opposes the prayer and submits that consent cannot be adduced from any of the statements given by the prosecutrix, be it under Section 161, 164 of Cr.P.C. or before the Court.
It is pointed out that prosecutrix has clearly mentioned that she was given an injunction so make her unconscious and thereafter appellant had performed illegal activity of violating her privacy.

It is submitted that as per the law when prosecutix was not in her senses and was dragged, then it cannot be inferred that she had given her voluntary consent for the establishment of physical relationship.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that in paragraph-86 of the case of Mahmood Farooqui (supra), Delhi High Court has clearly mentioned that incapacitation because of alcohol consumption, may not be taken as consent.
In the present case, prosecutrix has clearly mentioned that she was given some injection, as a result of which, she had become unconscious.
In view of this fact, it cannot be said that prosecutrix had given active consent to the appellant to violate her privacy.
Thus, the judgment rendered by Delhi High Court in the case of Mahmood Farooqui (supra) will not be applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.

In the case of Tukaram and another (supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that if trial Court after appreciation of evidence records a finding of acquittal, then reversal of the acquittal is not justified if the view taken by the trial Court was reasonably possible even though High Court was inclined to Virendra Gour vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173215386/
2 take a different view of the facts.

sentences.text: In view of such facts, when there is a direct evidence in the form of DNA report pointing out that appellant is the violator of the privacy of the prosecutrix and consequence is positive DNA report, in the opinion of this Court, at this stage, aspect of consent without appreciating the evidence of each and every witness cannot be inferred merely as the suggestion of learned counsel for the applicant.
Its a matter of trial whether there was an active consent of the prosecutrix or not and is not required to be seen at the stage of deciding the bail application.
Accordingly, this second appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
